title: the Ashtavakra Gita complete
hook: the last chapter is one small word asked over and over: where?
carry: the medicine has done its work

segments.voice: Yesterday, the great idler, in whom the straining stops, and the sage's hardest line: forget it all. Today, the last chapter.
screen: `THE ASHTAVAKRA GITA.` · `FORGET IT ALL.` · `TODAY: THE LAST CHAPTER.`

segments.voice: Kva. In Sanskrit it means where. It's a small word, the kind a child uses looking for a lost shoe. And the last chapter of the Ashtavakra Gita is built almost entirely out of it. Verse after verse, Janaka asks where. Not where is my kingdom, or where did I leave the keys. He asks where the things are that this path spends so long seeking. By the end, the word has asked about nearly everything, and the book simply stops.
screen: `KVA: WHERE.` → `VERSE AFTER VERSE.` → `THEN THE BOOK STOPS.`

segments.voice: Here's the shape of it, in paraphrase. Where are the elements, Janaka asks, where is the body, the senses, the mind, for me, spotless by nature? Where is scripture? Where is knowledge of the Self? Then the line that stops a reader short: where is bondage, and where is liberation? A verse later: where is the karma already begun, where is freedom while living? Those are the very ideas the Vivekachudamani ended on. Bondage and liberation have carried this whole book. Janaka asked about freedom on the first page; the sage told him he was free if he took himself as free. Now, at the end, the student isn't celebrating his freedom. For what he is, even bound and free have nowhere to stand. That's why it's a where and not a no. He isn't saying scripture is wrong or liberation a myth. He looks for them in awareness itself, and finds nothing there that needs them. On this reading, the medicine has done its work, and the bottle can go back on the shelf. So, the book in large steps: a king asks how to be free; a sage says he already is; the king cries out in wonder; the sage tests him; the book says forget even the book; and the king's last word is where. It also closes this year's lineage track, three roads in turn. Karma: the Gita's chapters on action, and a year of service designed. Bhakti: the Gita Govinda, the Bhagavata's tenth book and the kirtan songs. Jnana: the Vivekachudamani and this book. Each with its own voice, none asked to stand in for the others. Tomorrow the path turns to practice again, starting with the breath.
screen: `WHERE IS THE BODY, THE MIND, SCRIPTURE?` · `WHERE IS BONDAGE? WHERE IS LIBERATION?` · `A WHERE, NOT A NO.` · `THE BOOK IN SIX STEPS.` · then, large: `KARMA, BHAKTI, JNANA.`

segments.voice: Borrow Janaka's small word and ask it gently, without hunting for answers. Where is the body? Where is the mind? Where is the one who is trying to be free? After each where, rest in the quiet the question leaves.
Kva. Where. In the last chapter of the Ashtavakra Gita, Janaka asks it again and again, even of bondage and liberation.
Your line: the medicine has done its work. Three roads walked, each in its own voice. See you tomorrow.
